findings.failure_scenario: `mlflow.pyfunc.spark_udf(spark, uri, result_type=MapType(StringType(), StringType()))` on a `list[dict[str, str]]` model (including the PR's own `test_spark_udf` case): the model returns `[{"a": "b"}, {"c": "d"}]` for a 2-row batch; `pandas.DataFrame([result])` yields shape (1, 2), and `return result[result.columns[0]]` produces a 1-element Series, so Spark fails with 'Length of object (1) does not match with length of fields (2)'. Building the single column via `pandas.DataFrame({0: result})` matches the comment and the column-0 convention used on the input side.
findings.summary: For MapType results, `pandas.DataFrame([result])` wraps the whole list of dicts as a single row (shape 1 x n) instead of building a single column of dicts, so the UDF returns a length-1 Series for an n-row batch.

findings.failure_scenario: `mlflow.evaluate` or a direct `predict(pd.DataFrame({"input": [{...}, ...]}))` on a model hinted `list[SomePydanticModel]` (or bare `list[dict]`): the conversion now returns `[{"input": {...}}, ...]` instead of `[{...}, ...]`; strict pydantic validation then raises 'Failed to validate the input data against the type hint', and for bare `list[dict]` the model silently receives dicts wrapped under the column name. Old code unwrapped named single columns and worked.
findings.summary: `list(data.columns) == [0]` sends any single-column DataFrame whose column is not literally labeled 0 down `to_dict(orient="records")`, wrapping each element under the column name; the previous code unwrapped via `data.iloc[:, 0].tolist()`.

findings.failure_scenario: `spark_udf(spark, uri, result_type=DecimalType())` previously raised the documented 'Invalid spark_udf result type' MlflowException immediately; now the UDF is created and the error surfaces only mid-execution inside executors (e.g. 'Unsupported field type' or spark cast errors), or silently mis-typed output. The comment only justifies skipping the check for MLflow-inferred types, not for user-provided type objects.
findings.summary: `_check_udf_return_type` was moved inside `if isinstance(result_type, str)`, so user-supplied pyspark type objects (MapType, DecimalType, ByteType, non-string-key MapType, etc.) are no longer validated at spark_udf() call time.

findings.failure_scenario: A flat-signature `list[dict[str, str]]` model called as `pyfunc_model.predict(pd.DataFrame({"input": [{"a": "b"}]}))` (e.g. via mlflow.evaluate or serving): `_get_first_string_column` returns None for the dict column, `len(model_input.columns) == 1` is true, and `{"input": [...]}[0]` raises KeyError: 0 — the branch added to support non-string single-column inputs only covers DataFrames built by spark_udf (where the unnamed schema names the column 0).
findings.summary: The new single-column fallback `model_input.to_dict("list")[0]` indexes the result dict by the hardcoded label 0, so it only works when the DataFrame column is literally named 0 and raises KeyError for any other single-column name.

findings.failure_scenario: A spark_udf StructType result containing a nullable map field (e.g. a pydantic model with `optional_map: Optional[dict[str, str]] = None` omitted in one record, as the PR's own test does for `optional_int`) produces a None cell; the pandas branch then evaluates `None.items()` and raises AttributeError mid-UDF execution.
findings.summary: The new MapType branch of `_convert_struct_values` iterates `field_value.items()` with no None guard, crashing on null map fields, unlike the sibling primitive branch which was explicitly given an all-None guard.

findings.failure_scenario: A Bedrock Converse response with `toolUse.input = '{"location": "SF"}'` (a string, as the SDK returns for invalid JSON) now yields `ToolCall.arguments == '"{\"location\": \"SF\"}"'` — a quoted/escaped JSON string instead of the original JSON text — so any consumer parsing the recorded chat-trace arguments gets a string instead of the tool arguments.
findings.summary: `json.dumps(tool_call["input"])` double-encodes tool inputs that Bedrock returns as strings (documented behavior when the model emits invalid JSON), which the removed `input if isinstance(input, str) else json.dumps(input)` handled by passing the string through.

findings.failure_scenario: Maintainability: the same error-message text now exists in two modules; model.py's copy is never referenced anywhere (dead code), so future wording changes will drift between the two copies.
findings.summary: New `_INVALID_SIGNATURE_ERROR_MSG` constant is an unused duplicate of the identical message already defined and used in `mlflow/pyfunc/utils/data_validation.py` (line 22).
